name: SciTrends
license: No licence file and GitHub API license=null at commit 81711b9; paper is open access, which does not license the code.
permitted_use: Public source was inspected and executed in an isolated audit directory. No code or upstream data were copied into MedRadar. Only independently described methods and numerical audit findings are candidates for adaptation.
core_methods: Topic-year publication counts and five-year-ahead differenced targets
Lag, growth, review/original-research ratio and patent features
Ridge historical baselines and CatBoost regression with row-wise TimeSeriesSplit
Topic text embeddings in a separate lane
CRISPR patent/publication lag correlations
data_dependencies: Bundled trends_v6.csv.gz and derived context; PubMed yearly counts, review flags, patents and optional topic embeddings. MedRadar currently has zero collected USPTO patent rows.
accessibility: Official repository and bundled data accessible; no dependency lock or licence file; no release tags observed.

local_run.core_no_dl: 4,020 evaluation rows, 123 topics, 30 folds. CatBoost R2=0.845321, RMSE=153.694052; single-feature Ridge R2=0.196297. All 30 folds shared at least one calendar year between train and test.
local_run.crispr: 19 annual rows reproduced: same-year r=0.938010, future-patents shift(-1) r=0.887012; descriptive only.

resource_requirements: No GPU for the reproduced no-DL core. About 88 MB checkout, 97.1 MB CatBoost wheel, 4 CPU cap, 177 s wall time and 324,012 KiB maximum RSS reported by the logger. Embedding lane not run.
medradar_overlap: High for historical activity growth, lag/momentum and baseline comparison; no direct patent capability in the current frozen research lane.
transferable_methods: Five-year/lag growth features as candidates, not assumed predictors
Review-to-original ratio analogue only if a defensible regulatory event subtype exists
Compare nonlinear gains against persistence and simple linear models on identical cutoffs
Use publication and patent timings only when their knowledge times are defensible
limitations_and_leakage_risks: All 30 reproduced row-wise folds have train/test calendar-year overlap, so they are not clean public-time cutoffs.
Cell 34 mean-imputes using all X before CV; this leaks distributional information.
Stored notebook outputs differ for some Ridge lanes, indicating configuration/version drift; exact full-paper reproduction is not claimed.
CRISPR N=19 correlations are retrospective and do not establish patent lead time or forecasting skill.
No code licence; no upstream code or bundled data redistribution into MedRadar.
reproduction_status: author_core_no_dl_reproduced_with_documented_compatibility_fixes; embeddings and full-paper tables not reproduced

evidence.locator: README replication notebooks and official commit 81711b9
license=null, default_branch=main, size=32440 KiB
abstract and open-access article page
actual rerun metrics, data hashes and 30-fold temporal audit
actual 19-row lag recomputation

decision_reason: Growth and review-ratio ideas are testable on event histories, but only through an independent implementation with year-purged rolling origins, training-only preprocessing and explicit knowledge times. Upstream code cannot be integrated without a licence.

local_run.not_run: Full analyzer, corpus loader, PostgreSQL, Redis, web service, embeddings and end-to-end topic evolution.

Citation-year gain features only with point-in-time citation snapshots
Small algorithm tests isolated from service infrastructure

actual isolated fixture output

name: NIH iSearch Analytics
license: Public NIH documentation; no project-specific open-source licence or downloadable implementation was located.
permitted_use: Study public algorithm descriptions and historical cases only. Do not infer unpublished scoring details or claim access to NIH's internal model/data.

Historical backtesting narratives for CAR-T, mRNA vaccines and PrEP behavioral research
Linked publications, grants, patents, trials and approved drugs in iSearch

accessibility: Search-indexed NIH documentation is accessible in excerpts. Direct HTTPS retrieval failed in this environment with an SSL handshake error. Historical case titles and the 2–12 year prediction claim are corroborated by NIH sources; full scoring detail remains unavailable.

local_run.reason: No NIH-specific implementation, training snapshot or sufficiently detailed scoring specification was available. The unrelated sequence-clustering rMLC literature was not substituted for NIH's method.

resource_requirements: Unknown for NIH's full pipeline; likely substantial corpus processing. No local GPU, paid resource or new crawl was used.
medradar_overlap: Moderate for cross-source topic emergence and historical case validation; low until MedRadar has point-in-time publication, patent and grant data.

Evaluate predictions against dated historical cases rather than displaying current clusters
Preserve links to seminal papers and supporting evidence
limitations_and_leakage_risks: The public page names rMLC but the reviewed evidence does not disclose enough to implement NIH's scoring unambiguously
Historical showcase cases can suffer selection and hindsight bias
Current full-corpus clusters are not historical knowledge states
A 2–12 year claim requires frozen forecast registries and matured windows, not retrospective narratives

evidence.locator: NIH search-indexed description naming Recursive MultiLevel Clustering
NIH FY2025 congressional justification: more than 35 million publications and 2–12 year prediction claim
Historical case index: CAR-T, mRNA vaccines and PrEP behavioral research

decision_reason: The historical evaluation concept is valuable, but NIH-specific scoring and data are not reproducible from the public evidence reviewed. Do not build an rMLC lookalike and label it the NIH algorithm.

name: FDA AI 医疗器械纵向研究
license: Public JMIR/PMC article and supplementary tables. FDA registry and underlying device records are documented as publicly available at no cost; no special code licence is needed for independent statistics.
permitted_use: Independently compute statistics from public aggregate counts and cite the paper. Do not imply that manufacturer-level or device-level analyses were rerun without their rows.
core_methods: Four-era specialty distribution and annual authorisation rates
Specialty Herfindahl–Hirschman Index with 2000 bootstrap resamples
Cochran–Armitage trends with 17-test Bonferroni correction
Chi-square/Cramér's V with 10,000-replicate permutation check
Manufacturer-type logistic, cluster-robust and Firth sensitivity analyses
data_dependencies: 1,430 authorisations from the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Devices List downloaded 2026-03-01, decisions through 2025-12-31; 17 specialty panels and 576 manufacturers. Public supplement supplies complete 17×4 aggregate counts.
accessibility: Article, public FDA source documentation and Europe PMC supplementary DOCX accessible. The original PMC download returned a CAPTCHA HTML page, so the official Europe PMC supplementaryFiles API was used instead without bypassing access controls.

local_run.result: HHI=[0.181406,0.427424,0.738128,0.611688], chi-square=328.013095, Cramér V=0.276514, 51 expected cells<5, permutation p=0.00009999, radiology Z=5.300241, cardiovascular Z=-3.435419. Era4–Era3 HHI=-0.126439; this seed gives two-sided bootstrap p=0.001.
local_run.not_run: Manufacturer regressions, device-level duplicate audit and MedRadar migration were not run from aggregate data.

resource_requirements: Existing Python/pandas/SciPy/python-docx only; about 5.81 s wall time and 128,144 KiB max RSS; no GPU or paid resource.
medradar_overlap: High for descriptive concentration, specialty diffusion and small-sample robustness. It can inform H6, but current missing MedRadar event/specialty tables prevent migration claims.
transferable_methods: Report HHI with bootstrap intervals rather than a point alone
Separate recent era-specific increases from significant monotonic trends across all eras
Use permutation checks for sparse contingency tables
Apply cluster-robust/small-sample sensitivity when firms contribute repeated devices
limitations_and_leakage_risks: Descriptive evidence category 1, not evidence that HHI predicts later diffusion
Four eras are unequal and ordinal trend scores are not annual causal effects
Updated submissions are distinct authorisations, not necessarily unique products
Lower-volume manufacturer classification partly uses founding year/naming conventions; technology-company OR rests on only 13 devices/5 firms
Aggregate supplement cannot validate entity resolution or manufacturer regression

evidence.locator: Methods, Table 1, statistical analysis, limitations and public data statement
Public DOCX Tables S1–S8 used for independent recomputation
Actual independent HHI, bootstrap, trend, chi-square and permutation results

decision_reason: The aggregate methods are transparent and independently reproduced. Adapt HHI/uncertainty/sparse-table robustness to versioned MedRadar specialty panels once raw mappings are available; do not convert descriptive diversification into a forecast.
